stories.title: Fix mode hot-reload so `heare mode <name>` takes effect on a running daemon
stories.evidence: DeciderProcessor._reload_mode() reads ~/.heare/mode and sets settings.mode. Called from process_frame before every decider dispatch. 3 tests in tests/test_mode_hot_reload.py verify: (a) writing silent then ambient flips between suppressed and active decider calls, (b) missing mode file is a no-op, (c) garbage mode string is ignored. All pass.
acceptanceCriteria: DeciderProcessor re-reads ~/.heare/mode before each decider call (or on a short interval)
Changing ~/.heare/mode from ambient to silent causes the next transcript to be logged but not trigger a decider call
A unit test creates a temp mode file, constructs DeciderProcessor, asserts the decider call is skipped when mode is SILENT, then writes ambient to the file and asserts the next call proceeds
Plan §7 Step 10 claim about hot-reload is now actually true
Existing 48 tests still pass

stories.title: Fix silent-timeout: AWAITING_CONFIRMATION cancels after N seconds even if user stays silent
stories.evidence: DeciderProcessor._schedule_timeout_task / _timeout_watcher / _cancel_timeout_task. On transition to AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, a background asyncio task sleeps confirmation_timeout_seconds and calls _cancel_pending under the lock. On yes/no/timeout, the task is cancelled. 3 tests in tests/test_silent_timeout.py verify: (a) silent timeout with no frames cancels to LISTENING, (b) yes response cancels the timeout task, (c) no response cancels it. All pass. Existing frame-triggered _check_timeout path still works and its existing test still passes.
acceptanceCriteria: When DeciderProcessor transitions to AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, a background asyncio task is scheduled that fires _cancel_pending after confirmation_timeout_seconds if the state has not changed
The background task is cancelled if the user responds (yes/no) before the deadline
A unit test drives the processor into AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, waits longer than the timeout without sending any frames, and asserts state returned to LISTENING and pending_action is None
The existing frame-triggered _check_timeout path still works and still has its test green
No spurious cancellations when the user responds quickly

stories.title: SIGTERM handler actually cancels runner.run(pipeline)
stories.evidence: main.run_until_stopped() wraps runner.run(pipeline) and heartbeat.run() in asyncio.Tasks and uses asyncio.wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) across them plus a stop_event. On SIGTERM, the handler sets the event; stop_waiter wakes up, the finally block cancels the runner and heartbeat tasks and awaits them. _cmd_start delegates shutdown to this helper so the logic is unit-testable. 2 tests in tests/test_shutdown.py verify: (a) SleepingRunner is started and cancelled when SIGTERM is raised, (b) QuickRunner completion also triggers heartbeat shutdown. Both pass.
acceptanceCriteria: main._cmd_start wraps runner.run(pipeline) in an asyncio.Task that the signal handler cancels
HeartbeatTask is also cancelled (via stop_event or Task.cancel)
store.close() and pid_file.unlink run on the finally path
A unit test starts _cmd_start with a FakePipelineRunner (one whose run() sleeps forever), triggers the shutdown path programmatically, and asserts the task is cancelled and cleanup ran
If the unit test is infeasible for the full _cmd_start flow, factor the shutdown handling into a helper that IS unit-testable and test the helper instead

stories.title: Log rotation: ~/.heare/logs/daemon.log rotates at 10MB
stories.evidence: main._setup_logging installs a RotatingFileHandler with maxBytes=10*1024*1024 and backupCount=3 (DAEMON_LOG_MAX_BYTES / DAEMON_LOG_BACKUPS constants). 2 tests in tests/test_log_rotation.py verify: (a) _setup_logging returns a RotatingFileHandler with the correct thresholds and creates the log file, (b) actually writing enough bytes through a small-cap handler produces a .1 backup file. Both pass.
acceptanceCriteria: main._setup_logging installs a RotatingFileHandler with maxBytes=10*1024*1024 and backupCount >= 3
A unit test writes enough bytes through the configured logger to trigger rotation and asserts a .1 backup file appears
Plan §6 Phase E criterion 'daemon.log exists, rotates at 10MB' is now verifiable without a 1-hour soak test

stories.title: Edge-tts general network failure is caught, not crashing the pipeline
stories.evidence: EdgeTTSService.run_tts catches edge_tts.exceptions.NoAudioReceived AND general Exception around the Communicate.stream loop. On failure: warning/exception logged, TTSStoppedFrame emitted from finally. 2 tests in tests/test_edge_tts_errors.py verify: (a) RuntimeError raised immediately yields only TTSStoppedFrame, (b) mid-stream ConnectionResetError yields partial audio then TTSStoppedFrame. Both pass.
acceptanceCriteria: EdgeTTSService.run_tts catches edge_tts.NoAudioReceived AND general Exception (network error, DNS failure) around Communicate.stream
On failure: warning logged, TTSStoppedFrame still emitted so the pipeline recovers
A unit test patches edge_tts.Communicate with a stream() that raises RuntimeError('network'); asserts run_tts yields exactly one TTSStoppedFrame and logs the error
Plan §6 Phase E criterion 'edge-tts network failure: speak short error chime (or silence), log, continue listening' is met

stories.title: Groq STT rate-limit back-off: document handling, add settings cap
stories.evidence: src/rate_limit.py defines RateLimiter with configurable clock+sleeper. Settings gained claude_max_calls_per_minute (default 30). ClaudeCLI._run awaits self._rate_limiter.acquire() before every subprocess spawn. 3 tests in tests/test_rate_limit.py verify: (a) under-limit calls have no sleep, (b) the 4th call over a 3/60s limit sleeps exactly 50s (earliest call at t=0, now at t=10 → wait = 60-10=50), (c) window pruning frees slots after the window elapses. All pass. README §Rate-limit caveat documents the tradeoff: Groq STT runs inside pipecat and isn't rate-limited by heare — we limit our own claude_cli calls which are the biggest cost center.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings gains a groq_max_requests_per_minute field (default 60) that we track via a simple in-memory counter in ClaudeCLI or a new RateLimiter helper
When rate would be exceeded, log a warning and sleep until the next minute (do not crash)
A unit test fires 5 calls at the limited helper with limit=3 and asserts the 4th and 5th are delayed until the window resets (using a mocked clock)
Comment the limitation in README troubleshooting section

Design note: Groq STT runs inside pipecat's GroqSTTService, so enforcement is best-effort — we mainly rate-limit our own claude_cli decider calls which are the biggest cost center. Document this tradeoff.
